pass-a-0.title: A girl with a red balloon
pass-a-0.source_detail: 영일중 2학년 배부물 「Lesson 5 More Reading」 — 교과서 밖 외부지문
pass-a-0.body_text:
Have you ever seen this image of a girl with a red balloon? It was painted by Banksy, a world-famous street artist from the UK. His artworks are known for carrying social messages about issues such as war and inequality. Even though he is internationally well-known, nobody knows his real identity, and this adds to his mystery. His art appears on streets, walls, and bridges, and is often created without permission.

Girl with Balloon is one of Banksy’s most well-known works. It originally appeared on a wall in London’s South Bank under Waterloo Bridge in the early 2000s. However, it is actually part of a series of paintings. In this artwork, a small child is reaching out toward a red balloon. There are different interpretations of the painting. According to one, the red balloon symbolizes childhood and everything it represents—such as innocence, dreams, and hope. If you think about it that way, the painting can be seen as a symbol of losing those things. The image is simple but has a strong emotional impact. That may be why so many people like it.

pass-a-1.title: Dr. Schofield, a Foreigner Who Loved Korea
pass-a-1.source_detail: 동아(윤정미) 중2 Lesson 6 READING 본문 — Dr. Schofield, a Foreigner Who Loved Korea
pass-a-1.body_text: On February 28, 1919, a man came to Dr. Schofield’s house. A man: Dr. Schofield, I have a special favor to ask you. Dr. Schofield: What can I do for you? A man: Many people are going to gather tomorrow for the independence of Korea. Could you take pictures of the event and share them with the world? At 2 p.m. on March 1, Dr. Schofield was hiding in a building and saw a large group of people gathering outside. He began to take pictures. Dr. Schofield: Unbelievable! There are so many people here. I hope the world will learn about this important event through my pictures. Do you know Seok Hopil? His English name was Frank W. Schofield, but he loved his Korean name. It sounded similar to his real name, and it also had a good meaning. Dr. Schofield was a Canadian doctor, and he first came to Korea in 1916 to teach medicine. He wanted to teach in Korean, so he began to learn Korean right away. He studied so hard that he was able to teach in Korean after only a few years. He believed that every country has the right to be independent, so he helped the Korean independence movement. On March 1, 1919, Dr. Schofield heard people shouting for Korean independence in Tapgol Park. He took pictures of the event with his camera. He then wrote an article about the historic event and sent it to foreign newspapers with his pictures. Dr. Schofield’s fight for Korean independence didn’t stop even after the March 1st Movement. He continued to write about the terrible situation in Korea for foreign newspapers. He was under the watchful eye of the Japanese police, so he had to go back to Canada in 1920. In 1958, he returned to Korea at the invitation of the Korean government and never left again. For the rest of his life, he worked hard to help Koreans, especially poor students. Dr. Schofield died in April 1970, and he was buried in Seoul National Cemetery.

pass-a-16.title: L6 ReadMore-2
pass-a-16.body_text: Frank W. Schofield was a Canadian doctor. He loved Korean people and helped the Korean independence movement. He took pictures of the March 1st Movement and wrote an article about it.

pass-a-17.title: L6 ReadMore-3
pass-a-17.body_text: Kim Mandeok was born in Jeju-do in 1739. She was a successful businesswoman. In 1795, she saw many people dying from hunger. So, she bought rice with all her money and gave it away to poor people. Her love for others was so selfless that many people respected her. From her life, I learned that selfless love for others can make a big difference.

pass-a-28.title: Street Art in London-1
pass-a-28.body_text: Modern street art comes in many different forms, and it makes cities colorful and lively. Today, we are going to see some well-known street artworks in London.

pass-a-29.title: Street Art in London-2
pass-a-29.body_text: The place that we are going to visit is Shoreditch. Poor workers used to live in this area, but now it is one of the hippest areas in London. We can find so many great pieces of street art here. Do you see the painting over there? It is by the artist STIK. He is famous for using only lines and dots in his paintings of human bodies. According to STIK, the three figures represent the past, present, and future of Shoreditch. Which figure represents which? Well, look closely at the eyes of the three figures. They are just dots, but they will give you a clue.

pass-a-30.title: Street Art in London-3
pass-a-30.body_text: We are now in Finsbury Park to see a painting by Banksy, an internationally famous street artist. Banksy’s artworks often carry social messages, and the green tree (that) you see over there is a good example. As you can see, he created a green tree by spraying green paint on a wall behind a leafless tree. Next to the tree, there is a person who is holding a sprayer. What message does Banksy want to give us through this painting? In many people’s opinion, he is telling usthat nature is having a hard time. They think (that) he wants us to take better care of it.

pass-a-31.title: Street Art in London-4
pass-a-31.body_text: The final stop of our tour today is Muswell Hill. Can’t see any street artworks? Well, look down and look closely. Do you see the little chewing gum paintings? They are by the artist Ben Wilson. Wilson is well known for painting pictures on gum that people drop on the street. His gum paintings often carry personal messages from people (that) he meets on the street. For example, the one over here is a happy birthday wish for a loved one. Wilson’s gum paintings are tiny, but they give great pleasure to many people.
